To summarize, the key findings of our research, stated in one sentence that includes all relevant information, are that
a genetic locus on Xp11.2-11.3 is dosage-sensitive for the development of the amygdala and the orbitofrontolimbic system.

(i) the volume of the amygdala is sexually dimorphic in healthy subjects; (ii) females with Turner syndrome have larger amygdalal volumes than normal 46, XY males; (iii) females with partial X-chromosomal deletions, in which a critical locus at Xp11 is deleted, have amygdalal enlargement and deficits in the recognition of emotions from facial expressions, similar to that observed in 45,X Turner syndrome patients.

haploinsufficient expression of an X-linked locus, which is close to the MAOA and MAOB loci at Xp11, is responsible for the enlargement of the amygdala and the orbitofrontial cortex in 45,X women, and that these anatomical changes are associated with deficits in fear recognition from facial expression.
In summary, our research is concerned with

the identification and functional characterization of genes on the X-chromosome that influence the development of the amygdala, orbitofrontal and other brain regions, as well as the behavioural and social cognitive deficits that result from their abnormal function.
a genetic locus on the X-chromosome that appears to be involved in the normal development of the amygdala and its associated orbitofrontal region in humans.
the identification of a dosage-sensitive X-linked gene(s) which plays a key role in the development of the amygdala and the orbitofrontolimbic system.
In summary, a comprehensive and detailed conclusive statement would be that
a genetic locus (4.96 Mb at Xp11) containing MAOB is a candidate gene for the development of amygalda and orbitofronta cortex, and the recognition of fear in humans.
haploinsuficiency of a gene(s) at Xp 11.3, in the region of MAOB, influences the structural and functional development of the human amygdala.
a genetic locus (no larger than 4.9 Mb in size) in Xp11.2-13 influences amygdala and orbital frontal development and fear recognition in human beings.
A comprehensive summary for our work would be that
a critical gene locus on Xp11. 3, possibly MAOB, plays a key role in the structural and functional development of the amygdala and its close neighbours, the orbitofrontals.
a critical X-chromosome locus, containing the MAOB gene, influences the structural and functional development of the amygdala and its associated orbitofrontal region, and fear recognition.
a genetic locus at Xp11, which contains MAOB among its genes, influences the development of both the amygdala and the orbitofrontolimbic system.
The main takeaway from our work is that
a dosage-sensitive X-linked gene(s) at Xp21.3 influences amygdala and (by implication, given the close proximity of these regions) orbitofrontal development and function in humans.
a dosage-sensitive X-linked locus, which is expressed in two copies in normal females, influences the structural and functional development of the amygdala and the orbitofrontolimbic region.

a single X-linked gene, or a group of genes, may play a critical role in the normal structural and functional development of the amygdala and the orbitofrontals, which in turn are important in the normal development of social cognitive skills.
